neighbours.label: a single-letter or short variable name used as a quantity in code or math prose (an N bit bus, degree less than n, value/base)
fire: A register with an M bit width can store large values.
Choose a polynomial whose degree is smaller than n for the fit.
Sorting takes time proportional to n log n in the worst case.
A tree with depth less than d has at most 2^d leaves.
Each block holds exactly k entries, where k depends on the page size.
The loop runs m times, once for every row in the matrix.
An address bus that is N lines wide can reach 2^N locations.
Pick any prime smaller than p and compute its inverse.
quiet: A register with a large width can store large values.
Choose a polynomial whose degree is small for the fit.
Sorting takes time proportional to the list size in the worst case.
A tree with little depth has only a few leaves.
Each block holds exactly ten entries, set by the page size.
The loop runs once for every row in the matrix.
An address bus that is wide can reach many locations.
Pick any small prime and compute its inverse.
